injected_omission.original:
# Text normalization

Requires Python 3; no third-party dependencies or installation needed.
Run commands from this directory.

## Command line

The CLI reads all stdin, strips leading and trailing whitespace, collapses
internal whitespace runs to one ASCII space, and lowercases the text.
It always appends exactly one newline.

```sh
printf '  HeLLo\t WORLD\nAgain  \n' | python3 cli.py
```

Output:

```text
hello world again
```

Empty or whitespace-only input prints just a newline (one blank line):

```sh
printf '' | python3 cli.py
printf ' \t\n' | python3 cli.py
```

## Library

```python
from normalize import normalize

assert normalize("  HeLLo\t WORLD\n") == "hello world"
assert normalize("") == ""
```

The library returns a string without adding a trailing newline.

## Verification

```sh
python3 -m unittest -v
```

Or run the test file directly:

```sh
python3 test_normalize.py -v
```

The tests cover normal and empty/whitespace-only input for both the library
and the CLI, including the CLI's exact trailing newline.
